CRUXES AND SURPRISES. (1) Allen dates Pseudo-Dionysius inconsistently across the volume: 'late fifth century' (4301, 7929), 'late fifth- or early sixth-century' (478-480), and 'sixth century' (9208, 9930, in essays 14 and 15). Recorded as open questions on three claims; a card must not choose a date on Allen's authority without saying which essay. The audit lead 'Dionysius called Proclus's disciple about line 9930' is confirmed (9930: 'Proclus' great sixth century disciple, Dionysius the Pseudo-Areopagite'). (2) Leads 11248-11256 confirmed: Ficino's Philebus commentary 1.26 gives a seraphic triad (head, breast, thigh) and, following the Divine Names 4.8, three angelic motions; both are Allen reporting Ficino, so attribution is scholar_report. (3) Leads 10941-10949 are notes citing the Birth Day essay pp. 87-91 and 89 (Orpheus, Pico's Commento III); I did not claim from them; the same Pico material is claimed here from the primary passage at 10576-10601, and R-ALLEN-1 will have the essay-10 statement, so a linker should treat the pairs as same_claim. (4) Note 28 (1597-1602) quotes Pico's Italian: the Platonists' 'son of God' is to be compared to 'il primo e piu nobile angelo da Dio creato'; this is Allen quoting Pico's Commento (not in the corpus), so the claim is scholar_claim, not primary_text. (5) The Ficino-Pico relationship claims tagged quarrel are Allen's characterisations (Commento attack on Ficino's Symposium reading; De ente dismissal of Parmenides/Sophist; Ficino annoyed at 'temerity'); Allen's fullest argument for the 'second Ficino-Pico controversy' is in his 1986 article, not in this volume, only cited at 1499-1503 and 4507. (6) The poliziano tag (claim on Eurydice etymology) concerns Poliziano's compliment to Ficino, not a Pico-Poliziano dealing; kept as 'other'. Lorenzo tag likewise ('Lorenzo's and Pico's scorn' for the failed Orpheus). No savonarola material beyond the two remarks in essay 1 (679, 751).
